newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fugitive French politician to return to face trial.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive French politician to return to face trial.

text.p: A fugitive French politician sentenced to jail for corruption in his absence while a fugitive in Argentina is due to return home voluntarily on Tuesday to face justice, judicial sources said on Friday.

Jean-Michel Boucheron, a former junior Socialist cabinet minister and mayor of the southwestern city of Angouleme, said earlier this month that he had given up fighting a French extradition request and would return home from South America.
Boucheron, 50, was sentenced to four years in jail in 1994 for taking bribes from utility contractors, fined and stripped of his civic rights for five years.

On his arrival, police would take Boucheron into custody in Bobigny near Paris before a judge ruled on whether he should stay in detention pending a re-trial. Anyone sentenced in their absence in France benefits from a re-trial.

Boucheron fled to Argentina in 1991 and opened a restaurant which has subsequently gone bankrupt. "You can't live with a sword of Damocles above your head forever," he told an Argentine newspaper on March 10, announcing he would return home.
